newsitem.title: USA: Civil rights groups challenge Calif. welfare plans.
newsitem.headline: Civil rights groups challenge Calif. welfare plans.

text.p: A coalition of civil rights groups went to court on Tuesday to prevent California from barring undocumented women from prenatal medical care.

The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) of Southern California, the Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund and O'Melveny & Myers said they sought a temporary restraining order from a U.S. District Court judge.
The restraining order would prevent the state from barring undocumented women from prenatal medical care under California's Medi-Cal program, the ACLU said in a statement.
California Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, said the ACLU legal action was "frivolous" and without merit.

Wilson said the new federal welfare reform act clearly states that illegal immigrants are barred from public benefits. He said the state would move "expeditiously" to implement the provisions of the act.

The ACLU said the threatened cut-off would jeopardize the health and welfare of pregnant women and their children, and dramatically increase the costs when these women are forced to obtain emergency health services.

The ACLU and other coalition members said California's attempt to bar undocumented women from prenatal care would violate an existing injunction against California's Proposition 187, which seeks to bar many services to illegal immigrants.
The coalition also claimed that the threatened action would violate the state Constitution.
